source.title: MIT team discovers that unrealistic training data makes AI climate predictions more reliable
source.text: MIT researchers have developed a method that lets AI climate models get by with a single training run instead of the usual six to eight. An algorithm generates deliberately unrealistic scenarios with extreme CO2 or methane swings that make the model more robust. Until now, these emulators were often outdated by the time they were finished, according to the researchers. The article MIT team discovers that unrealistic training data makes AI climate predictions more reliable appeared first on The Decoder .

draft.headline: MIT researchers found that training AI climate models on deliberately unrealistic data makes them more reliable.
draft.threads_post:
Feeding AI climate models wild, fake data makes their predictions more reliable, according to MIT researchers.

An algorithm generates deliberately unrealistic scenarios with extreme CO2 or methane swings to make the model more robust. That lets the AI finish in a single training run instead of the usual six to eight. Researchers say emulators were often outdated by the time they finished training.

Would you trust climate AI trained on fake extreme data?
